LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: how the main characters make the story flow. 1. How can you tell the main character in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

A. identify signs of the main characters in a class reader,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learners develop the skill of working collaboratively by sharing ideas on how the characters make the story flow.

● Critical thinking : Learners develop the skill of open mindedness and creativity to examine links while discussing predictions made

from the title and the section read.

Values:
● Responsibility: is enhanced as learners write a summary based on the main character.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the skill of intensive sign reading to their learning in Kiswahili or Kenya Sign Language
